title: CEO at Raymond James Financial

speaker: Paul Reilly
title: CEO at Raymond James Financial
msg: In the Private Client Group, next quarter's results will be positively impacted by the 3% sequential increase of assets in fee-based accounts. speaker: Paul Reilly
title: CEO at Raymond James Financial

speaker: Paul Reilly
title: CEO at Raymond James Financial

speaker: Paul Reilly
title: CEO at Raymond James Financial

speaker: Paul Reilly
title: CEO at Raymond James Financial

speaker: Paul Reilly
title: CEO at Raymond James Financial

speaker: Paul Reilly
title: CEO at Raymond James Financial

speaker: Paul Reilly

title: CEO at Raymond James Financial

speaker: Steven Chubak
title: Managing Director at Wolfe Research
msg: So we and others are admittedly scrutinizing some of these cash disclosures much more closely. Your disclosures note that Raymond James shares a portion of the revenue from sweep options with the advisor.

speaker: Steven Chubak
title: Managing Director at Wolfe Research

speaker: Paul Reilly
title: CEO at Raymond James Financial
msg: No, that's a great question. Let me explain the disclosure first. So on advisory accounts, cash has no different payment in terms of the advisor than any other asset class. speaker: Paul Reilly
title: CEO at Raymond James Financial
msg: If there's 5%, they're getting $10,000 in fees. There's no indirect incentives and trips or awards or points or anything. speaker: Paul Reilly
title: CEO at Raymond James Financial
